history.dynasty: Gupta-period attribution (6th-9th c. CE); Wikipedia places the complex in the Gurjara-Pratihara period, 8th-9th c. CE - verify
history.summary: The Hateshwari Mata Temple at Hatkoti village (Jubbal tehsil, Shimla district) stands at the confluence of the Pabbar river and the Bishkulti and Raanvati streams, on Sonpuri hill. It is the principal shrine of a stone temple complex of 6th-9th century CE temples built in the classical Shikhara/Nagara style (later partly rebuilt in Pahari style after damage from floods). The sanctum houses a 1.2-metre bronze/ashtadhatu murti of the goddess as Mahishasuramardini - eight arms, Mahishasura's head at her left foot - flanked by 7th-8th century inscriptions and a torana arch carved with Navadurga and Veenadhari Shiva. Legend says the goddess slew the demon Mahishasura here; some local claims count it among the 51 Shakti Peethas (UNVERIFIED - Sati's left leg said to have fallen here). The complex also has the adjacent Shiva temple (see seq 1577), five stone shrines said to represent the Pandavas, the 'chained kalash' (iron-bound copper vessel), a kirtan ghar, dharamshala, yagyashala and Satsang Bhawan. The original seat of the goddess is said to be at Kharshali (Adi Hateshwari) above Hatkoti.

town_description: Hatkoti is a village in Jubbal tehsil of Shimla district, on the banks of the Pabbar river about 100-102 km from Shimla town. It sits at the meeting point of the Pabbar, Bishkulti and Raanvati streams, a confluence regarded as a pilgrimage spot in itself. The Pabbar Valley here is known for trout fishing and angling; the Sawra Kuddu hydroelectric project (111 MW) is nearby. Hatkoti lies ~14 km from Rohru and is approached from Shimla via Theog, Kotkhai and Jubbal.
